subject: Consortium pricing question: Orbit Labs cohort credits
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma@orbitlabs.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consortium pricing question — Orbit cohort credits

Hi Mateo,

Quick intro — I’m Emma (Program Lead) at Orbit Labs. We’re running a spring cohort of 18 startups and a couple of our sponsors have asked whether Redwood can offer a consolidated promotional pack rather than issuing separate trial credits per team. Two asks from procurement: whether credit pools can be created at the cohort level, and whether there’s any multi-team discount for cohorts that commit to a reserved capacity within 90 days.

A few details:
- 18 teams, expected average usage 60M tokens/month per team in month 1 (spiky).
- Sponsors may top up a shared pool.
- Timeline: cohort starts July 15; they’d like pricing + contract terms in the next two weeks.

Attached a short SOW and a rough usage matrix (Orbit_Cohort_SOW.pdf).

Can Redwood do a pooled credit model and, if so, can you sketch discount thresholds for converting to Dedicated reserved capacity? If you need numbers I can pull more.

Thanks — Emma

Emma Chen
Program Lead, Orbit Labs
emma@orbitlabs.ai
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Consortium pricing question — Orbit cohort credits

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Orbit Labs request. High priority: cohort starts mid-July and procurement wants terms in two weeks. Key asks: pooled cohort credit, sponsor-topup handling, and a path to reserved capacity with discounts.

My initial thinking (for discussion):
- Offer a cohort-level pooled credit bucket (admin-owned by Orbit) with per-team caps to limit abuse (suggested cap: 150M tokens/team/month).
- Sponsor top-up accepted as prepay to the cohort pool; Redwood invoices Orbit as primary account and we map credits to teams in our ledger for reporting.
- Phased reserved-conversion discount: 10% off commit for first 3 months, 20% off if they sign a 12-month commitment within 90 days.
- Include a one-time migration credit (small) to cover prefix/KV cache cold-starts if they move workloads to Dedicated.

Questions for pricing/legal ops:
- Is 150M cap reasonable from an SLO/cost risk perspective?
- Can billing ops map sponsor prepayments to a single cohort account and still produce per-team usage statements for tax/expense?

I attached Orbit's SOW. If we can agree quickly I’ll send a clean proposal to Orbit with our suggested MOP and MAA.

— Mateo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Consortium pricing question — Orbit cohort credits

Thanks for the loop, Mateo. Good framing — a couple of adjustments from pricing & ops: 

1) Discounting: we can do a graduated discount, but recommend slightly different thresholds: 15% on a 6-month reserved commitment and 25% on a 12-month commitment (the higher floor helps justify the autoscale guarantees). The 10% starter feels too small to incentivize conversion.

2) Per-team cap: 150M is OK as a safeguard but propose a soft cap + overage billing rather than a hard block. That keeps teams running and reduces support churn. Overage rate should be explicit (e.g., committed rate + 30%).

3) Billing mapping: finance can accept sponsor prepay to a cohort account, but we need a sign-off from legal that sponsor funds are not treated as customer revenue in a way that affects recognition — Laura, can you confirm any contract language required?

4) Migration credit: ok to offer a one-time 50K-token migration credit per converting team (covers cold-starts and eval bursts).

If Orbit confirms team count and a rough baseline monthly aggregate (we need a 90-day projection), we can produce a two-option quote (Conservative and Aggressive) and an MOP + sample SOW.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with Orbit this week to run the proposal past them.

— Marissa

Hi Emma — thanks for the details and the SOW. We discussed internally and can outline a concise two-option proposal to present to Orbit Labs and your sponsors. Key points below; I attached a short one-page summary for procurement and a draft MOP (Orbit_Cohort_SOW.pdf).

Option A — Cohort Pool (no commitment):
- Cohort-level pooled credits owned by Orbit (admin controls).
- Per-team soft cap: 150M tokens/month; soft cap means teams continue generating with an overage rate (committed rate + 30%).
- Sponsor top-ups accepted as prepaid to the cohort account; Redwood invoices Orbit and provides per-team usage statements.
- One-time migration credit: 50k tokens per converting team.
- Validity: credits issued for 12 months from activation.

Option B — Phased Reserved Conversion (recommended for sponsors who want predictability):
- Cohort signs a reserved capacity commitment on behalf of willing teams.
- Discount schedule: 15% off list for a 6-month commitment; 25% off list for a 12-month commitment (applies to reserved units purchased).
- Conversion window: teams that convert within 90 days of cohort start receive an onboarding migration credit and priority provisioning.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable we’ll: (1) prepare a clean proposal (pricing table + sample SOW), (2) draft a short mutual action plan (timeline + PO milestones), and (3) share a DocuSign for sponsor signature/PO routing.

Would you be available for a 20-minute call Tuesday or Wednesday next week to review?

Thanks — looking forward to partnering.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Programs, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com
